changes.description:
feat(infra): deploy bougie-relay 0.1.7, which holds dropped shares for reconnect

Pins the relay built from cresset-tools/bougie-relay@bc15bf9b, the export of
the share-reconnect changes: a dropped share's URL is held for two minutes
for its owner to resume, viewers get a 503 "reconnecting" page meanwhile,
and TCP keepalive notices dead tunnels in about 30 seconds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: serve a repository at the root of a custom domain

A registry moving to sconce could not keep its URLs: every repository
lives under /{org}/{repo}, and the metadata's URLs are built from one
server-wide base. Mage-OS users have https://repo.mage-os.org in their
composer.json and its dist URLs in their lock files, so serving Mage-OS
from sconce needs that domain to be the repository.

A repository can now have a custom domain (migration 0059). A request
whose Host is that domain reaches the repository's Composer read routes
at its root: /packages.json, /p2/..., /dist/..., and the imported
upstream's own dist paths. Every URL in the metadata stays on the domain,
port included. Access is unchanged: credentials, anonymous access and
the update policy apply as on the /{org}/{repo} routes.

- Only those read routes exist on a domain. Publishing, uploads,
  snapshots and the APIs stay on the main host: anything else is a 404,
  and a write is a 405.
- The host is checked before any route matches, since Router::layer
  runs after matching and would leak the main routes' path parameters
  into a domain's request. The main host never needs a lookup; other
  hosts that are not a domain route as before. Only the Host header
  counts, never X-Forwarded-Host, so a proxy in front must pass it
  through (bougierepo's nginx does).
- `sconce repo-domain <org>/<repo> [<host> | --clear]` sets it. A domain
  is normalised to a bare lowercase hostname, and one hostname serves one
  repository. Nothing proves the caller controls the domain, so it is an
  operator command, not a dashboard setting: on a shared deployment a
  tenant who could claim any hostname could take over a domain its owner
  later points here. The dashboard shows it, and the repository page's
  install snippet uses it.

Verified against a local server with real Composer and no credentials:
a repository mirroring repo.mage-os.org, served at
repo.mageos.localhost, installs mage-os/language-nl_nl with its lock
file's dist URL on that host. repo.mage-os.org's original dist path for
3.5.0 serves the same bytes as the original (sha1 8c02df89). A publish on
the domain is a 405, and with anonymous access off a 401.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
